subject: ADR-152: a tool that only worked for the robot
body: A TOOL CANNOT FAIL MORE QUIETLY THAN BY RETURNING THE SUCCESSFUL ANSWER FOR THE OTHER CASE. collect-output is one of the 22 actions the page plugin PUBLISHES: it is in the manifest, every task may call it, and it is the only way to read what leaves a page through a Copy button, a download or a print. What it reads is window.__S, and window.__S was installed by tools/swarm.py as an init script on the context THE ROBOT BUILDS. Every other caller -- a task, an audit, a suite, a person driving the gateway by hand -- got a page with no capture on it, and the action answered '0 payload(s)': not an error, not a refusal, but exactly what a page that copied nothing says. 19 PAGES IN THIS KIT CARRY A COPY, DOWNLOAD, EXPORT OR PRINT BUTTON, 80 OF THEM IN ALL, AND NO TASK HAD EVER READ ONE -- and in this kit the button is the product: the collection sheet's Darwin Core export, the guide's .eco protocol, the ethogram's budget CSV, the deployment log's 'thing a reviewer asks for and the thing nobody writes down'. THE FIX puts the capture in harness_plugin_page beside the action that reads it, with swarm importing it rather than owning a second copy, and the plugin installs it BOTH as a context init script (so it survives open and reload) AND by evaluation into the page that is already open -- the ordinary case, where an init script added now would not run until the next navigation. Guarded, because a second install starts a fresh buffer, throwing away payloads nobody has collected yet, and wraps every wrapper around its own wrapper so each toast counts twice with nothing to say so. ONE MORE THING HAD TO CHANGE: the copy hook was installed on DOMContentLoaded, which is free when the script always runs before the document and means it is NEVER INSTALLED AT ALL when it runs into a page that has already loaded -- so the retrofit would have caught downloads and prints and quietly missed the one output most of this kit produces. verify_report 109 (+14) drives a fixture with the hidden-textarea Copy pattern every page here uses, a Blob download and a print, through a plugin built the way a task's runner builds one, and holds that the payload is TAKEN rather than copied, that the download is captured with its filename and not followed, that a second plugin installs nothing again, and that all of it survives a reload. mutate_report 64 (+7). THE SIXTH PAGE TAKEN WHOLE is deployment-log.html, the largest data-entry gap left since ADR-150 at 17 of 37 -- three instruments and a log whose product is mostly refusals: a sample rate that cannot survey bats, a card that fills before you come back, a clock 10.3 km of sound out, a converted camera that cannot produce NDVI, a logger reading its own casing. THE TWENTY FIELDS NOTHING HAD FILLED WERE THE RECORD FIELDS, which is not a coincidence: they carry no arithmetic, so no expectation ever needed them, and they are the entire point of a deployment log. 17 -> 37 OF 37 FIELDS, 101 -> 174 confirmed expectations, 101 -> 140 steps, and the kit 385 -> 405 of 520 (74% -> 78%). Six pages are entered whole: collection sheet, stand sheet, ecology lab, releve, experiment guide, deployment log. FOUR BRANCHES NOTHING HAD REACHED. The field sheet prints a coords line only when both latitude and longitude are there, and nothing had ever put either in. The firmware box emits a literal '?' into the log when blank, on a page that says in its own prose that firmware is not bookkeeping. The two skies the page treats as GOOD -- fully overcast and clear -- were never asked for, only the broken-cloud warning. And every GSD the task had ever held came from one of the three sensors on the dial, which fills all four optics boxes at once, so the four inputs beside it -- the ones a reader with any other camera has to fill in -- had never had a number put in them; typed by hand at 6.17 mm / 8.8 mm / 4000 px they give 2.10 cm/px, an 84x63 m footprint, 40 lines and 2,153 images, and wound up to 20 m/s the page refuses the plan outright, ONE IMAGE EVERY 0.47 S, a sentence no task in this kit had ever made it say. And the deployment CSV -- header and three rows, one per instrument -- is read off the Copy button by collect-output, the first output any task in this kit has ever held; the step after it holds that TAKING A COPY IS NOT AN EDIT. Every figure in the new steps comes from a Python oracle mirroring the page's arithmetic; none was typed by hand. HELD: 79 of the 80 buttons are still unread -- what changed is that reading them is now possible, which is a worklist, stated rather than done, and the obvious next slice; the capture is installed by the plugin, so it covers every route the kit actually uses and is not a claim about every possible one; collect-output reads what the page handed the clipboard API or the anchor, which is not a claim about the operating system's clipboard, and a page copying by a route none of these wrappers cover would still be silent -- the wrappers are named in one place now, which is the condition for widening them; and the flight row records the sensor's LABEL from the dial and the GSD from the numbers in the boxes, so with hand-typed optics those two describe different cameras -- the page has always done this and the task now holds it, which is the first step to deciding whether it should.
